To create a user in RHEL, use the `useradd` command. This command allows you to specify various options for the new user account.

For example, to create a new user, you can run:

```bash
[root@host ~]# useradd username
```

The `useradd` command has many options that can be used to define user properties. You can use tab completion to help fill in these options with minimal typing. For instance, typing `useradd --` and pressing **Tab** twice will display available options (Page 53).

Refer to Page 53 of the Red Hat System Administration I (RHEL 9.0) guide for more details on using the `useradd` command and tab completion.
